releases.bodyMarkdown:
**Breaking:** `Database.selectBytes` now returns a `BytesResult`
(`{Uint8List bytes, int rowCount}`) instead of a bare `Uint8List`. Update call
sites to read `.bytes` where they previously used the result directly.

- **New:** `selectBytes` reports `rowCount` — the number of rows serialized into
  the JSON. It is counted in C during the same serialization pass, so reading it
  is free: callers building a paging envelope (e.g. `has_more`) or logging a sent
  count no longer need a second `COUNT(*)` or to parse the bytes. The serialization
  hot loop is unchanged; the row count is a single store outside it, and the value
  rides along on the existing reader→main SendPort transfer.

```dart
final result = await db.selectBytes('SELECT * FROM events WHERE ... LIMIT 1000');
// result.bytes    -> Uint8List of JSON
// result.rowCount -> rows serialized (e.g. for has_more = rowCount == 1000)
```

Performance and observability release. No breaking changes, and no changes to the
public export surface — safe to upgrade from 0.5.x.

**Wins at a glance:** up to **~30% faster concurrent writes** on top of 0.5.0's
pipelining, a new diagnostics counter for native read-buffer memory, and automatic
reclaim of that memory after large-`selectBytes` bursts — bounding the RSS trade-off
0.5.0 introduced with native-view transfer.

- **New API:** `Diagnostics.readerJsonBufHighWaterBytes` — the summed capacity of
  every reader isolate's native `json_buf`, making the read-buffer high-water mark
  directly observable. Surfaces workloads that pin large native buffers after big
  `selectBytes` reads ([#183](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/183),
  [exp 183](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/blob/main/experiments/183-json-buf-retention-audit.md)).
- **Behavior change:** a buffered group of `execute()` calls that races
  `Database.close()` is now atomic — every call in the group either flushes or is
  rejected, never the old lock-order-dependent partial outcome. It still never hangs,
  and per-call success/failure semantics are unchanged ([#184](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/184),
  [exp 180](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/blob/main/experiments/180-group-commit-request-batching.md)).
- **Memory:** native read buffers that grow to serve a large `selectBytes` read now
  reclaim back to their initial capacity on the next small read, once a reader's
  `json_buf` exceeds 1 MB. A one-off concurrent burst of large reads (e.g. 8 × 8 MB)
  previously pinned tens of MB for the connection's lifetime; that high-water now
  settles back to ~64 KB. Warm large-read workloads keep their capacity (a 256 KB
  last-read guard prevents shrink-then-regrow churn) ([#183](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/183),
  [exp 183](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/blob/main/experiments/183-json-buf-retention-audit.md)).
- **Performance.** See the [interactive benchmark dashboard](https://danreynolds.github.io/resqlite/benchmarks/)
  for current cross-library numbers.
  - **Cross-call write batching (group commit)** — standalone `execute()` calls that
    pile up while a write is in flight now coalesce into a single cross-isolate
    request (each statement still its own autocommit), collapsing a concurrent
    burst's per-write round-trips toward two. −26% to −32% on the concurrent
    single-insert lane, on top of 0.5.0's pipelining; isolated and sequential writes
    are unaffected ([#184](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/184),
    [exp 180](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/blob/main/experiments/180-group-commit-request-batching.md)).

experiments.title: Single-row large-text bind encoder
experiments.summary: Revives exp 179's direct-ASCII `allocateParams` rewrite against a representative large-payload workload — the explicit revisit condition exp 179 named. Focused `single_row_large_text_bind.dart` measures **−15% to −32%** at 16 KB → 1 MB single-row INSERT text binds, reproduced across order-flipped passes; encoder isolation reproduces exp 179's −45% / −58% / −37% on the synthetic micro. Small-payload release-suite lanes (Parameterized Queries, Single Inserts, Concurrent Single Inserts) stay neutral, confirming exp 179's small-bind finding stands; the lone flagged batch-tx regression is sub-decision-threshold noise on a routing path the encoder does not touch (`allocateBatchParams`). Saves one `Uint8List` allocation + one byte-buffer copy per ASCII string param; non-ASCII strings still take the unchanged `_allocateParamsPreEncoded` fallback.

experiments.title: JSON buffer reclaim release coverage
experiments.summary: Measurement-support guard for exp 183: `SQLite Diagnostics` now emits `JSON buf (KiB)` and a `JSON buffer reclaim (8 large selectBytes + 64 small settles)` row. The row grows reader `json_buf` capacity with a concurrent large `selectBytes` burst, settles with small reads, and fails if post-settle retention stays above 512 KiB; the focused suite run settled at **64.0 KiB** with idle readers. Parser/sidecar/history data carry optional `jsonBufKiB` while legacy diagnostics tables remain parseable. No runtime code.

experiments.title: Writer residual re-split (post-159/180)
experiments.summary: Measurement: re-ran exp 147's `writer_sqlite_wall_audit` after pipelining + group commit landed. Breakdown essentially unchanged (A11c overlap SQLite 13.6% / invalidation 16.0% / residual 70.3%) — the audit is sequential and exp 180 coalesces only concurrent bursts. Retires writer-residual micro-opts: the residual is the SDK-gated per-write round-trip, invalidation precision is owned by in-flight exp 160 (#155), the dirty harvest (~4–6%, exp 182) is small, SQLite config is mined. No runtime code.

experiments.title: json_buf retention audit + high-threshold reclaim
experiments.summary: Diagnostic + reclaim. Adds `Diagnostics.readerJsonBufHighWaterBytes` (sum of per-reader `json_buf.cap`) so the bounded RSS high-water exp 174 left as a known trade-off is now directly observable. Pathological retention is real on a one-off concurrent-burst workload (8 × 8 MB `selectBytes` pins **32 MB** across the 4-reader pool for the rest of the connection's life) and on a recurring-large pattern (16 MB pinned). A high-threshold C-side `realloc` shrink — fired by the reader worker after `SendPort.send` on a `selectBytes` reply when `json_buf.cap > 1 MB` AND the just-sent result was < 256 KB — reclaims back to the 16 KB initial cap on subsequent small reads: **post-burst settle 32 MB → 64 KB** (×4 readers, summed); recurring-large **16 MB → 64 KB**. Neutral on the focused `large_bytes_transfer.dart` lanes (±2 % within run-to-run noise). The 256 KB last-len guard is what makes the policy safe under back-to-back large reads — they keep their warm capacity

experiments.title: Skip preupdate dependency tracking when no streams active
experiments.summary: Added a `track_dirty` flag on `resqlite_db` plus a `tracksDirty` field on writer requests so `preupdate_hook` and the reply harvest both short-circuit when `_streamEngine.length == 0` at send time, with a `DrainRequest` no-op barrier from `StreamEngine._createStream` to fence in-flight non-tracking writes before the new stream's initial query. Two order-flipped focused passes confirm the no-stream wins (sequential **−3.8% / −5.3%**, wide-batch **−2.4% / −5.9%**) but also reproduce a with-streams regression (`with-streams guardrail` **+2.7% / +3.7%**, classified `reproduced` by `ab_drift_check.dart`), and the Tracelite `stream-rerun-dispatch` decision came back `inconclusive` with all three stream-direction warmup elapsed regressing in the same direction (+12% / +36% / +21%, gated `too_noisy`). Reactive streams are the library's primary use case, so the workload mix where the optimization helps is narrower than the one it slows. Reverted from `lib/` and `native/`; focused harness retained; implementation preserved at `archive/exp-182`.

experiments.title: Single-stream long-payload hash
experiments.summary: Added a focused one-reader harness that removes exp 173's eight-stream reader-pool parallelism: one unchanged stream hashes 64 rows x 64 KB TEXT + 64 KB BLOB (~8 MB) before a queued `COUNT(*)` barrier can emit. Re-tested the 16-byte FNV fold against the exp 110 8-byte body across an order-flipped pair. Baseline medians were 2.771 / 2.777 ms; candidate medians were 2.763 / 2.792 ms (-0.3% / +0.5%), with fully overlapping ranges. Rejected: even isolated to one stream, loop unrolling is invisible on the public stream path. Native C reverted; focused harness retained.

experiments.title: Cross-call write request batching (group commit)
experiments.summary: The "group commit" lever exp 159 named: standalone `execute()` calls that pile up while a send is in flight coalesce into one `MultiExecuteRequest` (each statement its own autocommit — per-call semantics unchanged), collapsing a concurrent burst's N round-trips toward ~2 and capturing exp 147's ~72% per-round-trip residual that pipelining left behind. **−26% to −32%** on the release Concurrent Single Inserts lane, reproduced across order-flipped runs; sequential lane neutral (backpressure trigger adds no latency to isolated writes); the lone flagged nested-tx regression proven to be drift (sign-flip on an untouched code path).

releases.bodyMarkdown:
Performance and reliability release. No breaking changes, and no changes to the
public export surface — safe to upgrade from 0.4.x.

**Wins at a glance:** up to **45% faster concurrent writes**, **~1.8× faster large
`selectBytes` reads** (>256 KB), faster `Row` lookups and batch writes, a new
diagnostics counter for silent re-query fallbacks, and a reader-isolate crash fix
for `diagnostics()` under load.

- **New API:** `Diagnostics.unknownDependencyFallbackCount` — a cumulative counter
  of writes that conservatively re-queried *every* registered stream because native
  dependency tracking overflowed its caps (or hit OOM). Surfaces workloads silently
  paying full re-query fan-out on every write, which was previously unobservable
  ([#151](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/151)).
- **Bug fix:** `Database.diagnostics()` could intermittently crash a reader isolate
  (SEGV) when polled while readers were mid-query — it toggled SQLite memory
  accounting on live `NOMUTEX` reader connections. Read workers now bracket each
  request with a real busy guard, and diagnostics reports busy readers as a partial
  snapshot ([#156](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/156)).
- **Performance.** Each accepted experiment below; see the [interactive benchmark dashboard](https://danreynolds.github.io/resqlite/benchmarks/)
  for current cross-library numbers.
  - **Writer-request pipelining** over a persistent reply port — −36% to −45% on
    concurrent standalone writes ([#153](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/153),
    [exp 159](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/blob/main/experiments/159-writer-pipelining.md)).
  - **`selectBytes` native-view transfer** — sends a view over the reader's native
    `json_buf` instead of taking the sacrifice/respawn path; −44% (~1.8×) on large
    (>256 KB) byte reads, at a bounded ~+15 MB RSS ([#169](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/169),
    [exp 174](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/blob/main/experiments/174-selectbytes-view-transfer.md)).
  - **`Row.containsKey` identity fast path** — pointer-identity membership scan for
    interned keys on schemas ≤ 32 columns; −23% on the `containsKey` lane
    ([#173](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/173),
    [exp 176](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/blob/main/experiments/176-row-containskey-identity-fastpath.md)).
  - **`RowSchema` lookup fast path** — schema-name identity scan with `HashMap`
    fallback; ~2× faster main-isolate map consumption at 10K rows
    ([#150](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/150),
    [exp 158](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/blob/main/experiments/158-row-schema-hash-index.md)).
  - **Six-parameter batch packing** — extends guarded ASCII batch packing to the
    six-parameter shape; `executeBatch` p50 88 → 75 µs ([#141](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/141),
    [exp 149](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/blob/main/experiments/149-six-param-batch-packing.md)).
  - **Nullable batch packing** — nullable-aware packed batch encoder for first-row
    `NULL` text columns; nullable ASCII 10k×20 25.7 → 21.7 ms ([#145](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/145),
    [exp 150](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/blob/main/experiments/150-nullable-batch-packing.md)).

experiments.title: Single-row ASCII parameter packing
experiments.summary: Extended exp 125/149's direct-code-unit batch write to the single-row `allocateParams` path, removing the per-string `utf8.encode()` `Uint8List` + `encodedStrings` list for all-ASCII parameter lists. The focused `single_row_param_packing.dart` micro confirms the mechanism — encoder **−45% / −58% / −37%** on 1-short / 5-mixed / 1-KB ASCII shapes, flat blob+int control — but the full release suite is neutral (Parameterized +0.04%, Single Inserts −1.7%, 1 win / 0 reg / 166 neutral, the flags on untouched read paths). The bind is too small a fraction of any representative workload to register (exp 146 restated for single-row). Reverted from `lib/`; micro retained; implementation preserved at `archive/exp-179`.

experiments.title: Missing-benchmark-run declaration guard
experiments.summary: Measurement-only CI guardrail: `generate_history.dart` now fails the build when a chartable (accepted/in-review) experiment numbered `≥ 178` has no linked benchmark run *and* no `**Benchmark Run:**` opt-out declaration — converting the documented silent chart-invisibility failure (forgotten result file / date mismatch) into a loud error for new work. Reuses the existing `_skipsReleaseBenchmarkRunMapping` opt-out signal as the escape hatch; pre-178 experiments are grandfathered. No runtime code; `history.json` byte-for-byte unchanged

experiments.title: Order-flipped A/B drift discriminator
experiments.summary: Methodology tooling: mechanizes the JOURNAL's most-reapplied lesson (phase-ordered A/B gates confound code deltas with time-correlated drift). Adds `cvPct` + `classifyDriftFlag` to `benchmark/shared/stats.dart` and a `benchmark/ab_drift_check.dart` CLI that reads two order-flipped passes of per-run values and classifies a regression flag as `reproduced` (same-direction effect, comparable CVs), `drift-suspected` (CV asymmetry on the flagged phase, or sign reversal across the flip), or `inconclusive`. Re-run against the recorded flags from exp 159 (CV asymmetry) and exp 167 (sign reversal), it reproduces the verdicts those runners reached by hand. No runtime change; 14/14 unit tests pass

experiments.title: Row.containsKey identity fast path
experiments.summary: Routes `Row.containsKey` through the exp 158 schema-name identity scan (via a shared `RowSchema.containsName`) instead of always hashing the key in the private `HashMap`. For interned-key probes on schemas ≤ 32 columns the membership test becomes a pointer-identity scan; equal-but-non-identical keys and wider schemas still fall back to the map. Focused `row_map_facade` `containsKey` lane improves **~13.0 → ~10.0 ms (−23%)** with a flat `hot lookup` control, flipping Row from ~+3.6 ms slower than `LinkedHashMap` to at-parity. Behavior-identical, no public API change

experiments.title: Large selectBytes release coverage
experiments.summary: Adds a named `Large payload (~650KB)` `resqlite selectBytes()` row to the release JSON-bytes suite and curates it as `selectBytes() large bytes`, giving exp 174's native-view transfer path a release-history guard above the old 256 KB sacrifice threshold. Single-repeat release run measured 0.323 ms wall / 0.000 ms main for the new row.

experiments.title: selectBytes native-view transfer
experiments.summary: `selectBytes` sends a `Uint8List` view over the reader connection's persistent `json_buf` and never takes the sacrifice (Isolate.exit + reader respawn) path. Sacrifice is a real win for the rows path (zero-copy object transfer) but counterproductive for bytes — native JSON must be `fromList`-copied before `Isolate.exit` can transfer it, so it saved zero copies and only added a respawn, while the non-sacrifice path copied twice. **−44% (~1.8×)** on large (>256KB) byte reads by eliminating the per-query respawn, **−4%** on small, at a bounded ~+15MB RSS high-water. Net code removal, no public API change

experiments.title: 32 KB long-text streaming benchmark + 16-byte FNV fold
experiments.summary: Filled the open `long-text-stream-hashing` candidate by building the missing ≥32 KB cell workload, then tested an unrolled 16-byte FNV body inside `fnv_combine_bytes` against it. Two order-flipped passes showed the candidate consistently +4.5 % and +12.1 % vs the exp 110 8-byte body — slight regressions inside a 2.6 → 6.0 ms per-pass spread, no real signal. Premise refuted: at 32 KB on a pool-of-4 reader fleet the byte-stream fold is at most ~50 % of wall, so loop-overhead removal is below noise. C body reverted to exp 110's path; new `streaming.dart` 32 KB section, `workload_registry.dart` curated metric, and focused `benchmark/experiments/long_text_32kb_hash.dart` harness retained as the durable contribution.

experiments.title: Long-payload stream hash coverage
experiments.summary: Adds a default streaming-suite row for mixed 32KB TEXT + 32KB BLOB unchanged fanout plus long-BLOB hash correctness coverage. The mixed row lands at 3.446 ms median beside the existing 4KB TEXT row at 2.356 ms, closing the long-payload measurement blocker without justifying an immediate new hash-loop variant

experiments.title: Resolved runtime cache for `Database` hot paths
experiments.summary: Mirrored exp 159's `_sendPort` cache one layer up: a sync-readable `_resolvedRuntime` field on `Database` so post-open `select`/`execute`/`executeBatch`/`transaction` skip the `await _runtime` microtask hop. Two order-flipped passes on `writer_pipelining.dart` produced alternating-sign deltas inside per-round variance (sequential-awaited −2.3% / +2.5%, transaction-guardrail −7.5% / +6.1%, concurrent-burst +4–5% both passes). The theoretical ~1–2 µs/call saving sits at or below the focused-harness floor. No runtime code kept; exp 159's "the residual is the round-trip floor itself; further reduction needs group commit or a different transport" framing stands.

experiments.title: Synchronous uncontended writer mutex fast-path
experiments.summary: `Mutex.tryLock()` plus a non-`async` `Writer.execute` / `executeBatch` were a concrete request-scheduling attempt against exp 147's residual writer/request bucket. Paired focused + release runs showed the primary `sequential-awaited` / Single Inserts lanes within ±2 % (wrong direction), only Concurrent Single Inserts moved by −7.8 % — a lane exp 159 already drives at −58 % to −61 %. Sub-decision-threshold gain doesn't justify adding a slow-path branch plus the behavior change of sync-before-close writes no longer being rejected. No runtime code kept.

experiments.title: Tracelite workload-summary insight guard
experiments.summary: Adds a Resqlite-side validation step to `benchmark/profile/run_tracelite_profile.dart` so canonical profile runs fail if `tracelite explain` regresses to coverage-only output. The validated profile emitted dispatch floors, dispatch-bound point queries, work-bound merge rounds, tail spread, RSS, allocation, and WAL insight IDs; thin `workload_loaded` fixtures now fail locally

experiments.title: ResultSet.forEach consumer recheck
experiments.summary: Re-tested closed exp 141 after exp 158 on a real SQLite-backed consumer lane. The one-method `ResultSet.forEach` override had no stable current win: Pair A `forEach lookup` improved 30.525 -> 28.383 ms, but the longer confirmation reversed to 28.563 -> 30.942 ms, and `forEach length` also reversed. No runtime code kept; the focused benchmark remains for future result-shape rechecks.

experiments.title: EQP rowid dirty elision
experiments.summary: Replaced exp 134's custom SQL recognizer with SQLite `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` plus native dirty-row harvesting and a private plan cache, but the focused Tracelite initial-drain lane stayed neutral/inconclusive (`stream-initial-drain-rowid` -2.33%) and broader stream guardrails did not produce a stable keyed-PK win. No runtime code kept; implementation preserved at `archive/exp-164`.

experiments.title: Concurrent standalone writes release coverage
experiments.summary: Promotes the exp 159 send-gated writer-lock pipelining shape into release write suite coverage with a paired Single Inserts (100 sequential) / Concurrent Single Inserts (100 concurrent) row pair; resqlite concurrent median drops from ~2.9 ms to ~1.1 ms on the new lane (−58% to −61%) while sequential, batch, wide batch, and transaction rows stay untouched. Makes future writer-scheduling experiments evaluable on a public release lane without relying on the focused `writer_pipelining.dart` script

experiments.title: Writer request pipelining + persistent reply port
experiments.summary: **−36% to −45%** on concurrent standalone writes (new focused burst benchmark) by holding the write lock only across the send and letting the worker's port FIFO pipeline requests; persistent reply port + cached SendPort + sync completers remove a port allocate/register/close cycle and two scheduling hops from every write round-trip. Stream-dispatch Tracelite guardrails neutral on the clean order-flipped pass; exp 147 `residual_us` drops on all four audit workloads

experiments.title: Row schema hash index
experiments.summary: Adds a schema-name identity fast path for schemas up to 32 columns plus private `HashMap` fallback for `RowSchema` lookup; focused `select_maps` main-isolate consumption improved 0.169 → 0.081 ms at 1K rows and 1.998 → 0.967 ms at 10K rows while point-query throughput stayed neutral/noisy

experiments.title: Synchronous writer response resolution
experiments.summary: Switching writer response futures to `Completer<T>.sync()` was a concrete request-resolution attempt against exp 147's residual writer/request bucket, but the formal Tracelite stream-dispatch A/B did not clear the primary gate. High-cardinality fanout changed +2.92%, keyed-PK subscriptions changed +18.5% with too-noisy evidence, and many-streams writer throughput changed +14.0%. No runtime code kept.

experiments.title: Nullable batch parameter packing
experiments.summary: Makes the guarded packed batch encoder nullable-aware for first-row `NULL` text columns; focused nullable ASCII 10k x8 improves 13.552 → 11.152 ms and 10k x20 improves 25.738 → 21.723 ms while existing ASCII/Unicode wide guardrails stay neutral

experiments.title: Six-parameter batch packing
experiments.summary: Lowers the guarded ASCII batch-packing threshold to the Tracelite merge-round shape; profile `merge_rounds` improves executeBatch p50 88 → 75 us and writer SQLite time 87,895 → 75,947 us while keeping 2-3 parameter batches generic

experiments.title: Reader reply batching
experiments.summary: Batching stream re-query replies reduced the exp 136 completion counter in a profile smoke (A11c overlap completion callbacks 4,527 → 1,425, completion wall 109.6 ms → 55.6 ms), but the formal Tracelite stream-dispatch A/B did not produce a measured-elapsed win. High-cardinality fanout changed +5.18%, many-streams writer throughput +3.28%, and keyed-PK subscriptions +13.5%. Do not merge worker-side reader-reply batching without a workload that turns the callback reduction into end-to-end wall improvement.

experiments.title: Writer SQLite wall split
experiments.summary: Measurement-only: profile-mode writer responses now report SQLite-facing write time back into `ProfileCounters`; on A11c overlap, SQLite is 15.7 ms / 166.8 ms (9.4%), invalidation is 18.8%, and residual writer/request wall is 71.8%. Keyed-PK shows the same shape (18.1% SQLite, 18.7% invalidation, 63.3% residual). Clears the writer-wall-vs-SQLite-wall blocker; next stream work should reduce completion/reply scheduling or residual writer/request wall rather than SQLite-step tuning

experiments.title: Lower batch packing threshold
experiments.summary: Tracelite A/B run over `narrow-batch-insert` collected clean baseline and candidate histories but produced no primary improvement: resqlite changed +1.45% with neutral verdict, while the sqlite_async guardrail was too noisy. Keep the exp 125 large-wide-batch guard; small/narrow batches stay generic until a new workload proves parameter encoding is material.

experiments.title: Inline stream flush dequeue
experiments.summary: Replacing `_flushQueue`'s `take(...).toList()` dequeue and `availableWorkerCount`'s `where(...).length` with inline loops kept dispatch counters at zero but produced mixed wall-time signal: A11c overlap trended better, keyed-PK trended worse, and the active stream bottleneck remained elsewhere. No runtime code kept.

experiments.title: sqlite3mc 2.3.2 → 2.3.5 bump (SQLite 3.51.3 → 3.53.2)
experiments.summary: Satisfies exp 090's revisit trigger (SQLite `.2`+ point release with sqlite3mc tracking it); tests stay green including embedded-NUL + Unicode bind regression suite; release-suite single-pass A/Bs swing between 19/18/124 and 30/2/129 — Concurrent Reads 8× is the only metric that flags consistently across reruns (+~20% on a sub-ms metric) and is the focus of the soak window; FP-rounding hazard skipped because resqlite never serialises REAL via `sqlite3_column_text`

experiments.title: Tracelite profile insight audit
experiments.summary: Measurement-only: pinned Tracelite profile runs show stable dispatch floors (reader 12 us, writer 16 us), point queries at the dispatch floor, merge rounds with 77 us of floor-subtracted work, and memory/allocation signal that wall time alone hides; current `tracelite explain` only reports coverage, so richer workload-summary insight rules are the next measurement-system improvement

experiments.title: Single-row text parameter direct encoding
experiments.summary: Tracelite retest over `chat-sim` and `narrow-batch-insert` did not clear the primary gate: resqlite changed +6.86% and +16.4% with neutral/inconclusive verdicts. Do not carry the `allocateParams` direct UTF-8 path unless a future workload shows single-row string binding is material.

releases.bodyMarkdown:
- Added open-scoped SQLite extension loading via `Database.open(extensions: ...)`
  and `ResqliteExtension`, plus companion package wrappers for SQLite Vector
  and SQLite JS.
- Added declarative open-time extension setup with `onRegister`, writer/reader/all
  connection scopes, and `SqliteVectorIndex` helpers for SQLite Vector's
  `vector_init`.

experiments.title: Completion-side reader-handler counter
experiments.summary: Measurement-only: profile-mode counters (`completion_handler_us`, `stream_emit_us`) expose the main-isolate reader worker port handler chain on A11c overlap as 28.57% of total wall (burst + drain) at ~18 µs per call across 4,228 calls/burst, with subscriber emit only 0.35% of the chain. Reader-reply batching is the natural bounded implementation candidate. Closes the `completion-side microtask scheduling cost counter` entry in `signals.json#stream-rerun-dispatch.blockedOnMeasurement`

experiments.title: Keyed PK dirty rowid elision

releases.bodyMarkdown:
- **Behavior change:** `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is now applied by default on every connection ([#77](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/77)). Code that relied on FK constraints being silently ignored will now see them enforced.
- **Column-level reactive invalidation.** Streams now record the columns they read and writes record the columns they touch; a write to a column no stream watches no longer dispatches re-queries. Adds public `TableDependencies` / `TableDependency` / `TableColumnDependency` types ([#48](https://github.com/danReynolds/resqlite/pull/48)). +82% on disjoint-column writer-throughput benchmarks (A11c).
- Further write-path and stream-dispatch wins: cached BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK statements, inline-packed parameter buffer, direct batch parameter matrix encoding, FIFO reader-pool dispatch with bounded synchronous stream admission. See the [interactive benchmark dashboard](https://danreynolds.github.io/resqlite/benchmarks/) for current cross-library numbers.
- Documented that streams over virtual tables (FTS5, R-Tree, JSON1 `json_each`, etc.) don't get reactive invalidation; use `select` instead.

experiments.title: Concrete reader-pool stream admission
experiments.summary: Initializes `StreamEngine` with a concrete `ReaderPool` so `_flushQueue` stays synchronous and bounded by `availableWorkerCount`; tests now use diagnostics for stream registry size, and post-rebase profile counters stay at zero parks/retries/max-parked on A11c overlap and keyed-PK workloads

experiments.title: Invalidation traversal cost audit
experiments.summary: Measurement-only: profile-mode harness reports `invalidate_us` / `intersection_us` as a fraction of writer-side burst wall on A11c (baseline / disjoint / overlap) and keyed-PK. Overlap invalidation is 10–15% of wall (column intersection 2.5–5.7%); keyed-PK 13–14% (intersection ~4%); disjoint 22–23% only because column elision shrinks the denominator. Per-entry intersection probes are 80–200 ns. Extracts shared `audit_workloads.dart` so this audit and exp 119 stay structurally comparable. Removes invalidation traversal from the active candidate list — the structural ceiling on smarter dependency tracking is ~3 ms / 25k probes per overlap burst

experiments.title: Bounded `_flushQueue` admission
experiments.summary: Cap stream re-query admission at `ReaderPool.availableWorkerCount` per call so synchronous over-dispatch can no longer pile up against `_dispatchWaiters`. `dispatcherParkedTotal` drops from 3,590 → 0 (A11c overlap) and 1,198 → 0 (keyed-PK); `max_parked` 46 → 0. Release suite: 9 wins, 0 regressions, including neutral high-cardinality fan-out (the exp-100 killer)

experiments.title: Post-FIFO dispatch pressure audit
experiments.summary: Profile audit shows wake retries stay zero after FIFO, while A11c overlap and keyed-PK streams still produce parked dispatchers; next dispatch work should target stream admission/completion

experiments.title: FIFO dispatch waiters with counter gate
experiments.summary: Replaces the shared reader-pool dispatch completer with FIFO one-shot waiters; exp 115 counters show wake retries drop to zero under overload

experiments.title: Named parameter support (`Map<String, Object?>`)
experiments.summary: Functionally complete and correct; 5-run focused harness showed wide-batch within noise (+2.7%). Deferred for v0.x launch: 12K-LOC change touching the entire write path for an ergonomics nice-to-have, with 6/7 write-path benchmarks trending slightly slower (monotonic direction = weaker than independent noise). Reopen if (a) community feedback shows named params are a real adoption barrier and a 5-run release suite confirms neutral, or (b) someone redesigns dispatch as two top-level branches in `run_batch_locked` instead of per-row inline dispatch. Implementation lives on the `exp-117-named-parameters` branch.

experiments.title: Wide batch insert release coverage
experiments.summary: Adds a 10k-row x 20-parameter mixed-type batch insert to the release write suite so parameter-width regressions are visible on the public benchmark path

experiments.title: Dispatcher park counters for `ReaderPool`
experiments.summary: Measurement-only: profile-mode counters (park-total, wake-retry-total, max-parked-concurrent) that quantify the parked-dispatcher path exp 105 / exp 114 targeted indirectly. Wake-retry/park ratio reaches 93 % at concurrency=32 (pool=4), the direct wake-amplification signal. Tree-shaken from release builds. Unblocks future dispatch-area experiments with a non-wall-time evaluation gate

experiments.title: FIFO waiter queue for `ReaderPool` dispatch
experiments.summary: First A/B pass (against pre-exp-106 baseline) showed −10 % to −32 % on streaming fan-out paths; rebasing onto main with exp 106 polish merged collapsed all targeted wins into noise. Exp 106 elides stream re-queries on the writer side before they reach the reader pool, so the parked-dispatcher contention this change targeted no longer fires under any release-suite workload. Implementation reverted; doc + benchmark artifacts retained as the durable record. Cherry-pickable from PR git history if a workload re-introduces sustained pool parking

experiments.title: Direct batch parameter matrix encoding
experiments.summary: Avoids the temporary flat Dart parameter list; 10k-row wide batches improve 14-26% in the focused benchmark

experiments.title: Fixed-length batch parameter flattening
experiments.summary: Focused benchmark medians overlapped after repeated A/B passes; any large-batch improvement was below the current decision threshold, so the simpler growable-list flattening stays

experiments.title: Nested-tx benchmark + revisit savepoint string cache
experiments.summary: Built the missing nested-transaction workload (shipped) and re-tested exp 102's archived cached-savepoint-string pattern against it. Even on the worst-case 50×-shallow-fan-out shape the cache landed at -9 % (below the ±17 % decision threshold); deep-5-chain was flat. Confirms exp 102 across a maximally stressing workload — per-isolate-round-trip cost dominates per-call savepoint allocations

experiments.title: Long-text stream hash benchmark + 8-byte FNV
experiments.summary: Adds a long-text unchanged-fanout benchmark and cuts its median latency by 76% with chunked byte-stream hashing

experiments.title: Inline-packed parameter buffer
experiments.summary: **−10 % to −16 %** on text-param INSERT workloads (Single Inserts, Batch Insert, No-Streams Write Throughput) by collapsing per-text/blob `calloc` into the reusable param-struct buffer and passing actual UTF-8 byte length so `sqlite3_bind_text` skips its internal `strlen`

experiments.title: Persistent selectBytes out-parameter slots
experiments.summary: Target selectBytes benchmarks stayed within noise, and memory/rss flags removed any case for permanent native scratch state

experiments.title: Column-level dependency tracking (re-attempt of 052 under A11c)
experiments.summary: **+82 %** on A11c disjoint writer throughput (3,956 → 7,201 w/s); overlap unchanged (4,477 → 4,581 w/s); overlap/disjoint ratio drops 1.132 → 0.636, the direct signature of writer-side dispatch elision

experiments.title: Raise reader pool worker cap (4→8)
experiments.summary: Regressed A11c writer throughput by ~31% under N=50 stream fan-out; the profile's reader-pool serialization bottleneck was actually throttling completion-side microtask churn. Cap=4 is correctly tuned.

experiments.title: Re-eval of exp 094 (dirty/read string reuse) under A11c
experiments.summary: Even under A11c fan-out (~50× amplification of read-set/dirty-set add traffic), deltas were within noise on every workload the change targets (disjoint +4%, overlap −2%, concurrent reads ±10% — all inside MDE_ci). Empirically validates 094's original "below noise floor" rejection.

experiments.title: Native nested transaction depth control
experiments.summary: Focused nested-tx benchmark showed at best a small savepoint-only improvement; realistic nested write cases were flat or worse, so extra native API surface is not justified

experiments.title: Cached SAVEPOINT/RELEASE/ROLLBACK TO strings on `_WriterState`
experiments.summary: Theoretically removes per-nested-tx `toNativeUtf8` + `calloc.free` pair, but the benchmark suite has no nested-transaction workload — no directly attributable signal, only run-to-run drift on unrelated read paths. Pattern-matches exp 095. Revisit if a deeply-nested-tx benchmark exists

experiments.title: Cached BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK statements
experiments.summary: **−13 % to −14 %** on Batched-Write-Inside-Transaction and Growing-Stream Invalidation by replacing `sqlite3_exec`'s per-call prepare+finalize with three persistently prepared transaction-control stmts

experiments.title: Bounded stream re-query scheduler
experiments.summary: Did not improve unrelated reads during fan-out and regressed high-cardinality stream fan-out by 103%

experiments.title: 8-byte-chunked FNV for byte-stream cells
experiments.summary: Structurally sound (folds 8 bytes per multiply on the long-text hash path) but benchmark-invisible — current streaming workloads carry only short cells (≤ 3–8 bytes) that bypass the new main loop. Same class as exp 071. Revisit when a long-text streaming benchmark exists

experiments.title: One-pass initial stream decode and hash
experiments.summary: 14-16% faster setup-heavy streaming benchmarks by avoiding the initial stream query replay

experiments.title: Direct batch parameter encoding
experiments.summary: Large batch medians only trended down; no accepted-level harness win and too much duplicate parameter-encoding code

experiments.title: Persistent writer result buffer
experiments.summary: The removable 16-byte calloc/free pair did not produce reliable write-path wins

experiments.title: Dirty/read table string reuse
experiments.summary: Focused dispatch was effectively flat and the full suite produced no wins; native branch/lifetime complexity is not justified

releases.bodyMarkdown: - Faster streaming fan-out and write-path marshalling. See the [interactive benchmark dashboard](https://danreynolds.github.io/resqlite/benchmarks/) for current cross-library numbers.

experiments.title: Alias cache entry's read tables instead of copying
experiments.summary: Below the measurement floor — savings ceiling was one `strdup`/`free` pair per cached table name per reader query (~hundreds of ns on a 1–3 table query). Work medians unchanged in 3-run A/B; tail regressions pattern-matched run-to-run variance (`noop` regressed as much as `point_query`, but `noop` never touches the changed path). Same class as exp 076

experiments.title: `wal_checkpoint=NOOP` probe in periodic checkpointer
experiments.summary: Premise invalid — exp-029 is hook-gated on `pages_in_wal`, not timer-gated. NOOP exists to report the frame counter the wal-hook already receives; adding NOOP would be a strictly additive header read with no empty-tick cost to amortize

experiments.title: sqlite3mc dependency bump audit
experiments.summary: No bump needed — we are already on the newest stable sqlite3mc (2.3.2 / SQLite 3.51.3, 37 days old). The only newer target (3.53.0) is a 12-day-old .0 release excluded by our known-regressions policy, and its changelog shows no hot-path wins. Revisit when 3.53.2+ ships

experiments.title: Deeply-immutable `ResultSet` for zero-copy isolate transfer
experiments.summary: Blocked upstream: Dart's `@pragma('vm:deeply-immutable')` requires all fields to be in a closed set that excludes `List<T>`, `Uint8List`, and any typed data. `ResultSet` / `RawQueryResult` are `List<Object?>`-centered and BLOB cells are `Uint8List`. Re-check when SDK #50068 (DI typed-data factory) ships

experiments.title: `SQLITE_ENABLE_SETLK_TIMEOUT` + `sqlite3_setlk_timeout` on every connection
experiments.summary: Downgraded from Accepted after 5-run confirmation: original single-run p99/max wins were noise (baseline outlier that never reproduced). Multi-run median shows p99 +74 % to +172 % worse and max +29 % to +529 % worse on writes; noop regresses even though it has no lock contention. Needs a concurrent-reader harness + shorter timeout to be evaluable

experiments.title: Reserved reader slot for reruns
experiments.summary: The queue is the real source of the `A11` / `A11b` win; removing the reserved reader regressed broader workload balance, especially `A7`

experiments.title: Late dispatch generation stamp
experiments.summary: Real partial improvement, but materially weaker than 083 because reruns still pile up inside `ReaderPool`

experiments.title: Stream rerun pre-dispatch queue
experiments.summary: Eliminates the measured `A11` / `A11b` reader-pool wait bottleneck by coalescing reruns before pool admission

experiments.title: Message-graph hand-off benchmark
experiments.summary: Current `ResultSet` / `Row` shape is already near-optimal for the shipped `select()` contract; materialized maps and binary row facades both lose on end-to-end total

experiments.title: Binary row result storage
experiments.summary: Transfer-side numeric scan wins collapsed once full main-isolate row consumption was measured; mixed rows regressed and point-query floor worsened

releases.bodyMarkdown:
- Initial release.
- Persistent reader pool with dedicated worker isolates and automatic sacrifice/respawn for large results.
- Reactive streams with table-level invalidation, result-change detection (FNV-1a hashing), and per-subscriber buffered controllers.
- Native C engine with connection pool, statement cache, JSON serialization, and cell buffer reuse.
- Dedicated reader assignment bypassing C pool mutex for point-query throughput.
- `selectBytes` for zero-copy JSON transfer to server frameworks.
- Transactions with read-your-writes semantics.
- Batch writes via `executeBatch`.
- Encryption support via sqlite3mc.

experiments.title: Cheap-check-first sweep (four small wins)
experiments.summary: **−13 % to −23 % on write benchmarks** from cached `sqlite3_bind_parameter_count`; pairs with three correctness-neutral fast-rejects on invalidation, hash, and subscription paths

experiments.title: Pre-bound statement cache
experiments.summary: Rejected in pre-implementation analysis: bind is ~0.3 % of re-query wall time (~50 ns per call). No measurable headroom even for a perfect implementation

experiments.title: Native-buffered hash for `selectIfChanged`
experiments.summary: **−39 % on unchanged-fanout benchmark**. Worker-side C hash (`resqlite_query_hash`) short-circuits stream re-queries before any Dart decode when the result is unchanged

experiments.title: Bulk `step_many` batched FFI for read path
experiments.summary: Same wall as exp 018: memcpy-in-C cost exceeds FFI-crossing savings. Text-heavy workloads regressed +38 %. Dart already reads directly from SQLite's text buffer; adding a C-side copy before Dart decode is strictly worse

experiments.title: Single-slot schema-cache fast-path
experiments.summary: Within noise: Dart's cached `String.hashCode` already makes map lookups fast enough that a one-slot bypass is below the measurement floor for the current suite

experiments.title: xxhash64 replacing FNV-1a for result change detection
experiments.summary: +75 % regression on stream invalidation: xxhash mergeRound is ~2× more ops than FNV's xor+mul, and our inputs are pre-hashed 64-bit values rather than byte streams (where xxhash wins)

experiments.title: MRU-first stmt cache scan + SQL hash filter
experiments.summary: Structurally sound but unmeasurable: benchmark suite uses ≤ 10 distinct SQLs so the cache never stresses the scan path

experiments.title: Zero-row-change short-circuit + persistent dirty buffer
experiments.summary: Removes per-write calloc/free pair and short-circuits empty dirty set to a const empty list

experiments.title: SQL fingerprint in stmt cache
experiments.summary: Deferred: proper normalization needs a ~300+-line SQL rewriter; `sqlite3_normalized_sql` takes a prepared stmt as input, not raw SQL

experiments.title: DDL schema_version watchdog
experiments.summary: Deferred: initial implementation shipped + reverted after CI flakiness. Root cause is a C-level stmt cache race with SQLite's auto-reprepare — needs its own design pass to invalidate cached stmts on schema version bump

experiments.title: Shrink initial values allocation (256→4)
experiments.summary: Caused +40-44% regressions; Dart VM has a fast path for `List.filled` that shrinking bypasses

experiments.title: Transparent single-row fast path in `select()`
experiments.summary: Insufficient headroom — most of 063's win came from return-type change (`Map` vs `List<Map>`) which can't be captured transparently

experiments.title: JSON1 re-evaluation (post-041/043)
experiments.summary: Our custom path now ≥ JSON1 everywhere; confirms 031 with larger margin

experiments.title: Drop redundant `sqlite3_clear_bindings`
experiments.summary: Provably-redundant call removed; simpler bind path with documented invariants

experiments.title: SelectOne fast path API
experiments.summary: +28-48% point query win measured but rejected to preserve lean API surface

experiments.title: Combined single-row FFI call
experiments.summary: Text pointers invalidated by `sqlite3_reset` — required the inline-copy approach explored later

experiments.title: Row count hint in schema cache
experiments.summary: Marginal wins (2/0/61) on repeated queries but below noise on primary paths

experiments.title: Short-string value cache
experiments.summary: +134-256% regression. Dart's `String.fromCharCodes` is uncatchable with any Dart-level cache

experiments.title: Preupdate hook batching for batch inserts
experiments.summary: Savings (~2ms in 50ms batch) below noise floor

experiments.title: Columnar typed arrays
experiments.summary: Memory win confirmed (75% for numerics, 10000x fewer GC objects) but below time-based benchmark floor; requires memory profiling harness

experiments.summary: macOS dylib profraw flush doesn't fire from Dart VM host process; needs CI pipeline with standalone C binary
